sources.note: Compares two training-free intent classifiers built from summary statistics of prefill-time activations against trained heads on the same features, and finds the trade-off is not accuracy but where each fails — trained heads win fine-grained distinctions, statistical ones give better uncertainty on mixed prompts and survive adversarial rephrasing that collapses the trained heads to zero.
sources.title: Training-Free versus Training-Based Intent Classification in LLMs: Accuracy, Robustness, and Failure Modes

sources.note: Triggers a safety intervention in image diffusion from the intermediate clean-image estimate rather than from the prompt, and spends optimization only from the first timestep where a violation actually appears — so extra test-time compute is incurred on unsafe inputs and benign latency stays flat as the budget grows.
sources.title: Test-Time Scaling for Safe Text-Guided Image Generation via Intermediate Clean Estimates

sources.note: Generates financial reasoning benchmarks from executable computation trees over real tables so that answers are correct by construction with no model in the labelling loop, exposes four independently controllable difficulty axes, and finds that unit and scale perturbations collapse the strongest model from 98.4 percent to 3.0.
sources.title: V-FiLLM: Verified Financial LLM Reasoning Benchmark

sources.note: Adds a Self-Reflection token that lets reasoning models recover from harmful output mid-generation, cutting harmful completion rate from 13.8% to 4.1%.
sources.title: Self-Reflection Improves Safety of Large Reasoning Models

instructions:
Write the wiki definition for 'adversarial robustness'.

The sources below are every archived paper and talk that mentions it. Define it as they use it: if they disagree, say so; if the term is used loosely, say that too.

`related` is the one part of the note nothing can work out on its own. The wiki already links entities that turn up in the same summary; what it cannot see is the neighbour a reader would actually want next — the generation before this one, the benchmark it was built to beat, the method it replaces. Name those. Leave the list empty rather than repeating what the sources already put side by side.

Rules:

result.definition: Whether a capability or a defence survives an input chosen to defeat it, and across 4 sources measured in a way that repeatedly separates methods that look equivalent. The archive's instances: two intent classifiers matched on accuracy diverge entirely under adversarial rephrasing, where statistical summaries survive and trained heads collapse to zero -- so the trade is not accuracy but where each fails; unit and scale perturbations on a financial benchmark collapse the strongest model from 98.4 to 3.0 percent; and a self-reflection safety mechanism holds under a specially designed adaptive attack without targeted adversarial training. One image-safety method makes the cost structure explicit by triggering only from an intermediate estimate where a violation appears, so the extra compute lands on unsafe inputs while benign latency stays flat. The corpus's standing point is that robustness is a property of the pairing between a system and an attack class, and that a defence untested against an attack with a different structure -- gradient-optimised suffixes rather than semantic jailbreaks -- has not been shown to transfer.
